title: Treasury Marketable Borrowing Estimates (Q2 2027 / Q3 2027), 15:00 ET
source: EST: canonical file written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09), reading the two proposals that named it (proposals/treasury-borrowing-estimates-2027-05-03.from-tic-annual-survey-final-2027-04-30.json and its refunding sibling). THE DATE IS UNCHANGED AT 2027-05-03 BUT ITS DERIVATION IS REPLACED, because the rule the proposal cited is wrong. The proposal derived the date from 'the FIRST WEDNESDAY of February, May, August and November'; measured against api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov auctions_query (fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200), whose announcemt_date field carries the refunding announcement itself, that rule MISSES 10 of the 48 refunding cycles from 2014-11 to 2026-08 — every cycle whose 1st falls on a Thursday (the announcement is then the last day of the PRIOR month, e.g. 2024-01-31 for the February 2024 refunding) and four of the seven whose 1st falls on a Friday (2019-02, 2019-11, 2024-11, 2025-08). The rule that fits 48 of 48: the announcement is the single Wednesday inside the window [the 30th of the prior month .. the 6th of the refunding month], which contains exactly one Wednesday unless the 1st is a Friday, in which case May has taken the later Wednesday (2015, 2020, 2026) and February/August/November the earlier (2019-02, 2019-11, 2024-11, 2025-08). May 2027 opens on a SATURDAY, an unambiguous class that is 8 for 8 in the record, giving the announcement Wednesday 2027-05-05; the estimates release is the Monday two sessions earlier, a pairing that holds 15 for 15 against the borrowing-estimate release dates read off Treasury's own press releases (treasury-borrowing-estimates-2026-11-02 ledger) and is restated for the current cycle on home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/financing-the-government/quarterly-refunding/most-recent-quarterly-refunding-documents, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 73,518 bytes): '(The next release is scheduled for November 2, 2026)' under Financing Estimates and '(The next release is scheduled for November 4 , 2026)' under the refunding. STAYS estimate: that page publishes exactly one cycle ahead, so no Treasury 2027 calendar exists to confirm against, and a rule-derived date is never self-confirmed by this lane
notes: The QUANTITY half of May-2027 refunding week: the 15:00 ET Monday release carries the Apr-Jun 2027 borrowing number and its revision, the assumed end-June cash balance, and the FIRST estimate for Jul-Sep 2027; treasury-refunding-2027-05-05 (est) allocates it across the curve 48 hours later. Impact LOW on this event's own measurement, which extends the sibling's rather than inheriting it: across 47 releases from 2015-02 to 2026-08 (dates derived from the Treasury auction API and validated 15/15 against the sibling's primary reads), the 26 that were not FOMC meeting-eves closed TLT 11/26 up at -0.005% (permutation p=0.978), IEF +0.006% (p=0.938), ^TNX +0.041% (p=0.935) — the sibling's n=8 null reproduced to three decimals and then tripled. 2027-05-03 is NOT an FOMC eve: the Fed's own published 2027 calendar (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-09) has April 27-28 and then June 8-9, no May meeting. The one thing that makes this edition non-boilerplate is that it is very likely a DEBT-LIMIT-CYCLE edition — debt outstanding was $40.0946T on 2026-09-04 against the $41.1T limit, and on trailing growth the headroom is gone somewhere between December 2026 and April 2027 — and the limit-cycle regime is where every large revision in the record came from. It is still not tradeable: split by statutory limit episode, the 14 limit-live releases closed TLT -0.286% (p=0.241), the largest effect anywhere in the study and not significant. READ IT, DO NOT TRADE IT.
